correctness.rationale: Integrating-factor conjugacy z(t)=e^{βt}m(t) transforms the upper Volterra obstacle into ordinary reflection z(t)=sup_{s≤t}[e^{βs}(ρ(s)−1)]_+. Consequently y=ρ−m and η=m+β∫m; complementary Stieltjes measure gives uniqueness. Weighted supremum is 1-Lipschitz uniformly; sharp constants are 2 for occupancy and 1+βT for η (endpoint attained as pulse start approaches zero). For time changes λ, memory difference is bounded by δ+2βBε and integration-by-parts/BV bounds yield local J1 Lipschitz constants. Shifted high pulses create unbounded terminal occupancy difference while J1 input distance≤h; duration-stretched pulses create terminal regulator difference βHh. For β=0 time-change equivariance restores global bounds. Independent step-input tests verified the sharp constants and pulse obstructions; general claims follow the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: Qualified PASS for exponential-memory-specific sharp constants and local-versus-global J1 phase. Wang–Chakraborty 2026 Theorem 3.5 and Propositions 3.10/3.13 supply the general well-posedness and unspecified uniform Lipschitz bounds, and Remark 3.11 explicitly leaves J1 regularity open. Reed–Ward–Zhan 2013 supplies generalized drift Skorokhod suprema, a known ingredient but not the stated two sharp moduli or both J1 obstructions. Other linear-drift stability theorems could imply part of the result.
residual_risks: The conjugacy to ordinary reflection is standard and not an originality claim; a preexisting general drift theorem might imply some sharp estimates.
The general nonexponential-kernel J1 question remains open.
